title: Birthdays
tomorrow: which days does Abuela keep every year, no matter what?

lines: THANKS FOR THE FACT OF THEM.
cards: Birthdays now come with a feed: a wall of quick messages, cake emojis, a story set to the same song as everyone else's. Nice, and gone by midnight. An older Catholic birthday habit is quieter.
It thanks God for the person. Not for what they did this year, not for their grades or their goals, but simply for the fact of them, here, alive.

teach.b: A psalm that Jews and Christians both pray says it to God directly, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "I will praise thee, for thou art fearfully magnified: wonderful are thy works, and my soul knoweth right well."
The verses around it say God saw a life before it was born.

teach.h: BEFORE I FORMED THEE, I KNEW THEE.
teach.b: Jeremiah hears the same at his calling: "Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee." So a birthday, in this light, is a thank-you for a life God knew first.

teach.h: A BLESSING, A MASS, A NAME DAY.
teach.b: Catholic families keep it in small ways: a blessing over the cake, a Mass offered for someone on their birthday, a name said out loud at grace. Some also keep a name day, the feast of the saint they're named for.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: you can thank God for someone without ever telling them, and you can thank God for yourself, too. That's today's line.

And it closes a run of seasons: the three days, fifty days of joy, come again, God on holiday too, the harvest, the book of the dead. A whole year, kept at home, from the Advent wreath to the candles on a cake.

how: Catholic families mark birthdays with a blessing, a prayer at the meal or a Mass offered for the person; some also celebrate name days, the feast of the saint a person is named for.

o: the feast day of the saint you're named for
a party to celebrate what you achieved
thanking God for the fact of a person's life

games.q: your friend says birthdays feel self-centered and she'd rather skip hers. what does today's teaching offer her?
o: it isn't about her achievements; it's thanks for her life.
she's right: humble people don't celebrate at all.
celebrate bigger, so nobody thinks she's sad.
games.why: the psalm praises God's works, and a person is one of them. a birthday thank-you points toward the giver, not the self.

practice: Bring to mind one person whose birthday is near, or your own. Say their name out loud, and after it, one plain sentence of thanks for the fact of them, not for anything they did.
If you pray, you can offer that thanks to God in your own words, then sit with the name for the rest of the time.

wordCard.voice: Birthdays. Thanking God for someone's life, the plain fact of them, known before they were born.

orig.note: Latin, from the psalm in the Vulgate: wonderful are thy works.

carryVoice: Here's the line: thank God for you, and for the people whose birthdays you'd never forget. Two weeks of seasons, done.
